title: How do we draw lines perpendicular to given lines on dot paper?
description: Two dot grids each show two segments. The board draws an upright line for a flat one, a flat line for an upright one, and swaps the steps for a leaning one. It finds that one segment needs a wider grid.
teaching_notes: One idea: to get a perpendicular on dot paper, swap the steps and change one sign. Perpendicular lines need not be one flat and one upright.

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q1
video_script.why: The child has met the square mark for perpendicular lines and now draws perpendicular lines on dot paper.
video_script.substitution: Take each given segment and find a line at a right angle to it, the same way as the example in the book, using the steps across and up between dots.
video_script.anchor: Two dot grids, each three dots across and four dots up, with two given segments on each grid.
video_script.payoff_line: Upright lines for the flat segment, and flat lines for the upright one.

final_answer.value: Upright lines for the flat segment, flat lines for the upright one, lines of 2 across and 2 down for the leaning one; the 2-across-3-down segment needs a wider grid
final_answer.spoken: upright lines for the flat segment, flat lines for the upright one, and lines of two across and two down for the leaning one

hold_back: Upright lines for the flat segment, flat lines for the upright one, lines of 2 across and 2 down for the leaning one; the 2-across-3-down segment needs a wider grid
maths_rules: a line perpendicular to a flat segment is upright, so it goes between dots straight up
a line perpendicular to an upright segment is flat
for a leaning segment, swap the steps across and up and change one sign: 2 across and 2 up gives 2 across and 2 down
for 2 across and 3 down, the perpendicular needs 3 across and 2 up, but the grid is only 2 steps across, so it needs a wider grid or a set square
perpendicular lines need not be one flat and one upright
video_script.design: The two grids stay on the stage. The new perpendicular lines are drawn one at a time in a second colour, with a small square at each right angle.
